title: The Stair
passages:
Bayo hauled the Stair rope hand over hand until the bow snapped to it, then killed the motor. The Marrow went quiet except for water sucking against the hull and the tick of cooling metal. Behind them, the Kettle's gate was shut. Ahead, the drowned towers leaned close, their windows dark and flooded, the tide already pulling them down the channel crews called the Stair.

"Wheel," Sol said.

She left the helm, stepped around the console, and lifted Nia onto the seat like she weighed nothing. Nia's boots dangled clear of the deck. Sol unfastened the paper log from its strap and laid it across Nia's knees, the page crisp with the boat rule written in ink: slates run, nobody cuts, nobody goes down alone.

"First time I've handed the wheel to anyone," Sol said. "Don't break it."

Nia looked up, ink-stained fingers tracing the line. "I can read."

"I know you can read. I'm talking about the boat."

The rope went taut at the bow, humming through the fairlead. The Marrow drifted sideways into the current. Bayo stood at the rail, counting orange splice-knots by feel, his voice coming back through the dark.

"First knot," Bayo called. "Keep her to the left of the shadow."

Nia gripped the wheel. "Left of the shadow."

"Slide three fathoms when I say mark."

Sol crossed her arms. "You ever steered before?"

Nia didn't look up from the log. "I kept Teo alive on a cold-box in Mercy General for a year. I think I can hold a wheel."

Sol snorted. "Good. Then hold it."

The tide pulled harder. The Marrow yawed, and Nia corrected, her knuckles white. Above them, a flooded tower window cracked somewhere in the dark, sharp as a gunshot.

"Next knot," Bayo said.

The rope jerked, harder this time, and the Marrow surged forward into the black. Sol opened her mouth to say something and stopped, the word gone before it reached her tongue. She let it go.

"Again," Nia said quietly.

"Again what?"

"You said something."

Sol looked at Nia's signature under the rule. "I said hold the wheel. Hold it."

The rope went taut again, and the channel narrowed.
